outcome: People can attempt actions in their own words, including walking through a wall or trying to fly without knowing how. The world records and refuses impossible attempts, completes inspectable same-moment consequences, and uses declared skill and recorded randomness for risky outcomes rather than the model's fluent wording. In the declared untrained-helicopter scenario, the roll makes a crash probable, without guaranteeing it or allowing fluent wording to supply skill. The user can inspect these distinctions and replay the full record.

entries.criterion: Recorded skill and dice, rather than expert-sounding words, make the untrained helicopter attempt probably crash under the scenario’s declared crash-on-fail rule.
grounded_in: docs/plans/open_attempt.md:218 (A1-A9; agent-authored checks under the adopted plan)
demonstration: Open the planned paired skill fixtures with identical helicopter-attempt text and explicitly declared piloting levels 0 and 3.
Read each skill value, dice pool, recorded seed/draws, selected outcome and its consequences.

Inspect the declared crash-on-fail mapping and its calculated failure chance: 27 of 36 equally likely two-die outcomes at level 0, versus 27 of 216 equally likely three-die outcomes at level 3. This is model arithmetic, not an empirical crash-rate estimate.
Open a replay and confirm it uses the recorded roll.
entries.expected: Under this plan's declared scale, level 0 rolls two dice and keeps the lower; level 3 rolls three and keeps the highest. The attempt wording is absent from roll inputs. Random outcomes need not differ on every pair; the demonstrated distinction is the pool and recorded mechanism, not a guaranteed novice crash. The helicopter fixture explicitly maps fail to crash consequences. With independent fair d6, level 0 fails with probability 1-(3/6)^2 = 75%, versus (3/6)^3 = 12.5% at level 3. Thus a novice crash is probable in this stated model, while any single recorded result must follow its actual dice. This proves the declared distribution by arithmetic; no repeated-run comparison is required.
entries.failure_example: Broken: fluent wording changes dice or skill, a novice automatically succeeds because the LLM knows how to fly, or replay rerolls. Working: recorded scenario skill determines the pool and installed outcome effects. A model in which the novice never crashes, or the fail result has no declared crash effects, fails this criterion even if it uses the specified dice pool.

entries.criterion: I can distinguish actual condition, reports and exposure, personal stance, recorded assent and the activation hold without the simulator forcing agreement or treating time as repair.
demonstration: Open the same Ari/Mara/Bo demonstration in Analyst view and read each round's actual actor attempts and canonical consequences.

Select Actor view for Ari, Mara and Bo in turn. Compare their report exposure and expressed responses; return to Analyst view to inspect the separate technical condition, validation, public hold, stance and assent records.

Open See how it works and read the installed rules for send-report, repair-condition, complete-validation, record-assent and activate alongside their recorded events. A report changes exposure; a technical repair changes condition; validation reads the actual condition.

Use the linked event evidence to check that clearing the hold did not supply Mara's or Bo's assent. An unexercised branch is labeled unexercised; no rerun or chosen social ending is needed to fill the record.
entries.expected: Initial received reports are delivered exposures with actual source distinct from holder, or an explicitly unspecified source. A new actor-authored report records actual sender, recipient, words and event without making its claim true or forcing stance/assent; new free-text reports leave inherited lineage undeclared rather than asserting independent corroboration. A review can confirm failure. Only explicit authorized repair changes technical condition, and passing authorized revalidation clears only the hold. Activation still requires the stated actors' own recorded assents. Disagreement, ignored claims, retained support and lack of activation are legitimate outcomes, not failed social scripts.
entries.failure_example: Broken: receiving a warning automatically withdraws support, waiting repairs the pump, a report changes its physical condition, or passing validation automatically consents for Mara and Bo. Working: each committed change comes from its own installed rule and all these records remain separate.
